blocks.text: greetings of peace (Salaams) to Rasulullaah ﷺ is more rewarding than setting slaves free. Having love for Rasulullaah ﷺ is more rewarding than both setting slaves free and wielding a sword in the path of Allaah." [^1]
Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab (RA) said, "Du'aas remain suspended between the heaven and the earth and no part of it ascends until you send salutations to Nabi ﷺ." [^2]
Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "All du'aas are stopped just short of the heavens until salutations are sent to Nabi ﷺ. It is only when salutations are sent to Nabi ﷺ that the du'aa is raised." [^3]
The Statements of Hadhrat Ali (RA) and Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) Concerning sending salutations to Nabi ﷺ
Hadhrat Ali (RA) said, "Every du'aa is held back until salutations are sent to Muhammad ﷺ." [^4]

Hadhrat Ali (RA) said, "The person who sends salutations to Nabi ﷺ a hundred times on a Friday will have so much celestial light on his face on the Day of Qiyaamah that people will wonder what great deed he carried out." [^5]
Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) said, "It is not appropriate to send salutations to anyone other than the Ambiyaa." [^6]
Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) also said, "For anyone to send salutations to anyone else is inappropriate unless it be to one of the Ambiyaa." [^7]
Istighfaar (Seeking Allaah's Forgiveness)
The Narration of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) Concerning the Istighfaar Rasulullaah ﷺ Made in a Single Sitting
Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) says that in a single sitting, they would count Rasulullaah ﷺ recite the following Istighfaar a hundred times:
"O my Rabb! Forgive me and accept my repentance, for verily you are the Most Forgiving and Most Merciful." [^8]
